attributes.description: Alerts when server-side request volume (Logs) drops by more than 50% in the most recent 15 minutes compared to the preceding 15 minutes, per project. A sudden traffic collapse can indicate a broken deployment, DNS misconfiguration, or an authentication barrier blocking users.
attributes.name: [Vercel OTel] Request rate drop (traffic collapse)

investigation_guide.blob:
## Request Rate Drop

### Triage Steps
1. Confirm the drop is real and not a monitoring gap: `FROM logs-vercel.logs.otel-default | WHERE vercel.project.id == "<project>" | STATS count = COUNT(*) BY vercel.log.source | SORT count DESC`
2. Check the most recent deployment for the affected project — a broken build, misconfigured redirect, or crashing middleware can prevent all requests from completing.
3. Check DNS and domain configuration if the drop is total (near-zero requests) rather than partial.
4. Cross-check the corresponding Web Analytics page view rate (see the page view rate drop rule) — if both have dropped together, this points to an issue reaching users (DNS, CDN, or a global outage) rather than a narrow backend defect.
5. Check firewall deny volume — an overly aggressive new WAF rule can silently block all legitimate traffic.

### Note
This rule compares the most recent half of the time window against the preceding half within a single query; it does not use `timeWindowSize` history beyond the configured 30-minute window.

### Escalation
A total traffic collapse (>90% drop) on a production project should page the on-call engineer immediately.

esqlQuery.esql:
FROM logs-vercel.logs.otel-default
| WHERE deployment.environment.name == "production"
// Split the window in half: "recent" (last 15m) vs "baseline" (previous 15m) to detect a drop within a single evaluation
| EVAL is_recent = CASE(@timestamp >= NOW() - 15 minutes, 1, 0)
| STATS
    recent = SUM(is_recent),
    baseline = SUM(1 - is_recent)
  BY vercel.project.id
// Minimum baseline volume to avoid flagging naturally quiet/low-traffic projects
| WHERE baseline > 5
| EVAL drop_pct = ROUND(100.0 - (TO_DOUBLE(recent) / baseline * 100.0), 2)
// Alert threshold: adjust based on expected traffic variance (e.g. lower for high-traffic apps with stable load,
// higher for apps with legitimately spiky/diurnal traffic patterns)
| WHERE drop_pct > 50.0
| SORT drop_pct DESC
| LIMIT 20
